name: Jazz House / Disco House
summary: House built for musicians, not just dancers: a live-feel kick (often carrying quiet off-grid ghost kicks), heavily swung 16th hats mapped straight from MPC swing settings (54-67%), congas/bongos and rim/ride 'conversation' language standing in for a drummer, and disco-house's flammed claps, offbeat open hats and sidechain-shaped shaker beds on the nu-disco side. Swing amount is the single biggest lever between the two lanes: disco house sits tight (54-58%), jazz house classic and deep cuts push toward 60-67%.

sounds.kick: Live-feel, not hard-clipped: humanized velocity across every hit, often with a quiet ghost kick slipped off the main grid (St Germain/MAW school); disco house wants it punchier and more clipped (Purple Disco Machine school).
sounds.snare: A clap (not a snare) carries 2 and 4 in almost every pattern, frequently preceded by a soft ghost note; disco house flams two clap layers a few ms apart; true ghosted snares appear only in the Moodymann/deep lane.
sounds.hats: Swung 16ths are the whole point — MPC swing 54-67% depending on approach; jazzy/deep patterns lean toward the shuffled top of the range, disco-house patterns stay tight and add a loud offbeat open hat instead of dense closed hats.
sounds.percussion: Conga/bongo call-and-response loops, rim skips and a ride used as a lead groove voice (not a wash) for the jazz side; continuous 16th shaker beds shaped like a sidechain release for the disco side.
sounds.cymbals: A single crash marks section starts or a disco string-hit stand-in; ride otherwise carries the groove, never washes it.

machines: Roland TR-909 — Kerri Chandler's 'Chandlerized' modified 909 (extended pitch/velocity range, subharmonic kick layer) defines the jazz-house kick and hats (owned)
Akai MPC60 / MPC2000 / MPC3000 — the swing template every pattern in this style maps to (owned)
LinnDrum / LM-1 / LM-2 — 80s claps and toms for the disco-house lane (owned)
Roland TR-808 — clap layering, cowbell accent (owned)
Roland TR-727 / TR-505 — congas, bongos, claves for the percussion loops (owned)
E-mu SP-1200 / Akai S900 — 12-bit resampling for dusty Moodymann/Theo Parrish textures (owned)
Simmons SDS — toms for disco-edit descending fills (owned)
